newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla, mulls disclosure rule in bond deals.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla, mulls disclosure rule in bond deals.

text.p: Underwriters, financial advisers and other particpants in Dade County bond deals will be asked to disclose before each issue whether they have potential conflicts of interests or are the subject of regulatory actions or inquiriies.
The new rules were debated Friday by the county's Budget, Finance and Public Trust Committee, and sent to the full county commission for approval at a Jan 21 meeting.
"We're clearly operating in a climate where there's a lot of public scrutiny in the public finance arena," commitee Chairman Jimmy Morales said.

He said the county manager's finance committee, which makes initial decisions in assiging underwriters to Dade bond deals, would send out letters prior to each deal, asking potential participants to list "problems with capitalization, conflicts of interest, possible indictments" and other woes.
"Deal by deal, it's our obligation to send that request out," Morales said.
Several dozen underwriters attended the meeting, but none spoke when asked if they had any comment on the proposed rules.

Several times recently, the county has removed members of its bond underwriting pool from deals becasue of questions about their involvement in an ongoing federal probe of public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County.
A lawsuit is still pending over the county's removal of the firm Guzman & Co from the underwriting team for a $450 million water-sewer revenue bond issue due to be priced next week.
The suit alleged that some county commissioners violated Florida's public meetings law by discussing the removal vote privately. It also said the removal was arbitrary.

County Commissioner Natacha Millan had advocated the firm's removal because of a letter circulated in November, accusing another firm that acts as a county financial adviser of violating municipal securities rules.

The letter was purportedly signed by company president Leo Guzman, who said the letter was a forgery and asked federal regulators to investigate. But Millan said Guzman should be removed because "there is a shadow cast upon this person."

The lawsuit was disclosed in the bond documents for the upcoming water-sewer deal. Assistant County Attorney Gerry Heffernan said the outcome of the litigation would not affect the validity of the bonds.
Guzman's attorney indicated at Friday's meeting that he would ask the county commission on Tuesday to reinstate the firm in the underwriting syndicate.
If the board does so, the bonds would be redivided among syndicate members, but the sale would not be otherwise affected, Heffernan said.
